Although the negotiation exercises were not graded, they were the most important part of the course, as they provided an opportunity to apply what you learned and revise weekly.

sections.content: The course covers a wide range of negotiation concepts, which are all very useful and practical. I won’t go into too much detail, since I think it’s best to go into the course blind.
sections.teaching:
Every week, during the first lesson we had a negotiation exercise, where we each have a secret role/objective, and then we negotiation with other students in the class. Then, during the second lesson, we see everyone’s results from the exercise and discuss, with the professor introducing the concepts that are relevant to the case.

Prof. Nason is a very fun professor and his classes were quite interesting. He often gives anecdotes from his own life and was very laid back, which made the whole experience quite approachable.
sections.grading:
Due to COVID, we had two term papers instead of exams. For the first one, we had to plan and execute a negotiation (could be anything) and write a paper analysing it using class concepts. For the second one, we had to analyze a negotiation of our own choice (in history or in a movie).

Grading:
Personal Negotiation: 20%
Negotiation Case Analysis: 25%
Negotiation Guide: 5%
Research Participation: 5%
Participation & Discussion: 25%
Attendance: 15%

Me:
Personal Negotaiton Case: B+
Negotiation Case Analysis: A
Attendance, Research Participation, Negotiation Guide: Full
Participation & Discussion: Unknown
Final Grade: A

Although he didn’t release the grading criteria until after the personal negotiation was due (would’ve been helpful if he gave it before), he did tell us how he graded the papers:
C range - wrong/very little use of class concepts
B range - correct/good use of class concepts
A range - going beyond class concepts or analysing the class concepts in further depth (e.g. counterintuitive findings)

As such, I think the grading was quite transparent and fair. For example, for my personal negotiation case, I didn’t use anything that went beyond the class concepts or analyze in that much depth, so a B+ is understandable. The case analysis was graded similarly, so I made sure to go beyond the class concepts for the second paper. Overall, I think he was quite generous with the grading, as I wasn’t expecting to get an A because my first paper was only a B+.

In my opinion, even if it was bad grading (which I don’t really think it is), this course is an easy recommendation, since it’s both fun and useful. The topics and concepts you learn are quite relevant to any negotiation and it was easily the most fun course I’ve taken in a while.
sections.workload:
The workload wasn’t that much besides the preparation for the negotiation exercises, which mostly just required us to read our role and case information (~7 pages). The reports have a word limit (1000 for the personal case and 2400 for the case analysis) and you have a couple of weeks to do each.

One thing to note is that you should only register for this course if you are willing to participate in the negotiation exercises. Since these exercises are a major part of the course experience, not putting in the effort is both a waste of your own time, and it also ruins the experience for others.

In one of the exercises, we had a team negotiation where we each had separate information, but there was one girl on our team that was muted with her camera off and barely responded to anything we asked. This ruined the experience (as it’s like talking to a brick wall), and we only learned that she had crucial information we didn’t have when the other team asked us about it.

However, if you are willing to participate (which is quite easy since the cases are interesting and fun), it is definitely a worthwhile experience.

sections.content: Tbh, I'd say most of the content is pretty useful and practical.
sections.teaching: Not a fan of his teaching style, too much useless talking.
sections.grading:
Absolutely shit, most ppl in the class got C range for the first essay which he didn't even give a clear instruction and grading rubric for it. Neither the second essay. Besides, participation takes a huge part of it but he only picks the students he likes (I personally think).

Final Grade: B
sections.workload: A lot of reading materials are required, one case study and one actual negotiation every week.

sections.content:
Real Business case study and negotiation practice every week, one lesson for hands-on negotiation and the other for evaluation. content is very interesting and related to business.

Slides and its concepts are not too hard, very easy to understand, the weekly negotiation usually helps in understanding the slides.
sections.teaching: Nason is the best instructor, funny and inspiring, people in the class are very interactive because of the negotiation activities, there is a weekly negotiation result review and you can compare your skills with others.
sections.grading:
Quite Nice already, as long as you attend lessons as part of the grade will be from a random negotiation result done in class.

Final is not too hard if you study well, overall difficulty is not too high.

Full attendance (as I enjoy the lesson quite a lot) plus above mean in midterm and final(maybe)?
Final Result: A
sections.workload:
Very Light, almost no assignment except you have to prep for next week's negotiation. Even you don't prep for it, it is also ok. But you may lose a chance to enjoy the fun of negotiating (chatting) with others.

Almost forgot there is some quiz in class but its so easy that you can do it without studying.

sections.content: The class is about improving the student's negotiation skills and focusses on practical negotiation exercises through case studies.
sections.teaching: The professor seems fantastatic! Young, dynamic and knowledgeable. But it is worthwhile to note that he is also rather strict when it comes to attending class and being on time.
sections.grading: I did not have the exams yet...
sections.workload: The workload seems quite light, especially for a four credits class. You just have to read a few pages of the book per week, but other than that, class requires very little preparation.

sections.content: The content is mainly about different negotiation strategy and how to apply it in daily life which is quite funny.
sections.teaching: The instructor is very funny. The course is not just about teaching the theory but there were negotiation practices every week that can help students have more understanding on what we learn and we can have fun during the practice.
sections.grading: The exam is quite challenging as you can not only memorise the theory but the most important is that you have to understanding! Understanding is the main point of having good grade on exam as many of the exam questions focused on application instead of memorisation.
sections.workload: I think the workload is quite little. As there were only two exam, one midterm and one final. And yet there were some simple quiz but it was just very easy if you study the case study well.

sections.content:
Content is fun -- every tuesday is a practice negotiation and every thursday is a discussion. This makes the lass very interactive and works well for lawyers who prefer to learn by doing!!

I have actually found the negotiation tactics in this class very useful already, which I didn't know if I would.
sections.teaching: Nason is a very enthusiastic teacher in negotiations. I have taken other classes taught by him, and this is definitely his best class to teach.
sections.grading: Grading is very fair -- only one midterm and one final. There are super easy quizzes most weeks about the negiation case, easy to ace if you read the case. Just be on time!
sections.workload: Not hard at all.

sections.content:
The content is fun and useful.

Every week first lesson starts with a mock negotiation and the next lesson will be revealing the results and discussion about the concepts. Also, it comes with personal stories and real life example of negotiations to help you to be a better negotiator.
sections.teaching:
Prof. Nason is a exceptional professor, as his teaching is captivating and you always want to listen to what he was teaching.

He is also humorous and interactive, and you will learn something through the jokes and laughs.

Moreover, the teaching is not only about powerPoint as he will also share personal or real life examples of those negotiations which you will definitely like to hear.
sections.grading:
The grading is great.

But as this is a 4-credit course, the grading of the course becomes relative more important than other courses.

I am not really doing well in negotiations overall (one out of all negotiations results will be graded).

I am only at the mean for midterm and slightly above in the final.

And I got a B.
sections.workload:
There's a two-question quiz for most negotiations and it will be quizzed before the mock negotiation. If you read the case which are distributed the class before, you will certain get a full mark.

Also, the preparation is important. Apart from reading the case, thinking about what tactics you will be using in the class in also important, this can help you get the best out of your negotiation result (better grades).

sections.content:
Each week starts with a mock negotiation and then a review and discussion of results in the next class. The course involves quite sufficient practical skills and theories within negotiations and can be applied in multiple scenarios.

I personally recommend this course regardless of what school you study in. Do note that the course gets a bit dull after mid-semester as the concepts become quite repetitive.
sections.teaching: Nason's teaching style is really interactive and passionate. I believe most students enjoyed his teaching.
sections.grading:
Midterm 30%
Final 30%
Neg results & guide 5%
Quizzes 5%
Participation and discussion 15%
Attendance 15%

I'd say the grading for this course is quite subjective since participation and discussion accounts for 15% of grading. However, having that in mind, your grades should be good as long as you participate in class and score 1 sd above for exams.

exams are tough btw.
sections.workload: Super light workload, just remember to read the negotiation cases before class.

sections.content: An in class negotiation exercise every week, and the other lesson was used as a review and going through the lecture slides. The content is very interesting.
sections.teaching: Funny and friendly professor.
sections.grading: I got a B+ for the course while I got the mean score in both the midterm and in the final exam. I achieved 100% attendance and have answered some questions in class for class participation. The exam is composed of both MC questions and a case study in which clear concepts towards the course materials is essential.
sections.workload: You are expected to read the case study (2-4 pages long) before each negotiation exercise.

sections.content:
Not much content, professor get simple key messages across.
It is sometimes depressing not to have learnt anything after 80 minutes of class beyond one single sentence.
sections.teaching: Enjoyable to listen to lecturer. Room conditions unfavourable.
sections.grading: The grading appears somewhat intransparent with regard to the participation component, as students never have name tags and very few questions are asked. This might be cause for concern. Generally, however, I have heard that grading would be rather fair, while skewed to participation.
sections.workload: The workload appears to be a appropriate for a course that provides 4 credits.

sections.content:
Very interesting and useful for life, you will not get bored during the course.
Esepecially the practice negotiations are great for learning.
sections.teaching: Very enthusiastic professor, he seems he is really into the teaching and enjoys the lectures.
sections.grading: Fair and with a good approach to the grading, not impossible to have a good grade with fair amount of studying.
sections.workload: Read cases, be ready and mindful during the lectures. You need to be able to cooperate with other students in the class , therefore you need to be prepared not to let them down

sections.content: A negotiation practice weekly. The content is interesting and useful. Knowledge learnt can be applied for daily usage.
sections.teaching: Nason is a very nice prof. He's teaching is fun and interesting. Materials and cases used are meaningful too.
sections.grading: I was a few marks below mean for midterm and 0.5 SD above mean for final. Skipped one negotiation practice in class. And got B at last. The grading is reasonable.
sections.workload:
the workload is okay. Have to read a case weekly to prepare for the negotiation practice. There will be a very short quiz to test on your understandings on the case.
One midterm and one final exam. Exams are not difficult. With MC and case studies. As long as u go through all the ppt and materials, that will be fine.

sections.content: The content is all about negotiation and the skills. Each Tuesday you will have to nego with others, and will review the result in front of whole class on Thursday. You learn from your experience and jot your notes. His ppt is kind of trash, they are used for Prof Nason's teaching but not revision.
sections.teaching:
His teaching is interesting!
But the professor sitting in the class i.e. Daniel to teach in the next sem is quite boring(he taught for one class)
sections.grading: My grade is bad. Perhaps I am really not a good negotiator. I dont think it is easy to get good grade as you have to provide your views and opinions in the midterm and final for the given nego cases.
sections.workload: The workload is to prepare and read the case before Tue class, or you will fail to negotiate with your classmate right away. And you may need to adjust your mindset to care less about the negotiation result if you are a poor negotiator like me

sections.content: The class is likely one of the most important classes you'll ever take in university. Teaches you a lot about negotiating and business behavior.
sections.teaching: Professor Nason is highly interactive and well-versed in Negotations. The class is interactive and requires you to throw out all self-reservations about engaging in class discussion. It will be you against another classmate once a week. It is war.
sections.grading: Nason is a tough, but fair grader. He'll give you about just as much as you put in. Stand up character.
sections.workload: You better show up for the weekly negotiation.

sections.content: You can learn a lot from Stephen, as he is really good at negotiation. The negotiation skills, principles, some theories will be taught. In most of the lessons, he will distribute cases for you to read one week before, then you need to do negotiation with one or more classmates, and afterwards you need to fill in the result sheet, this sheet marks as your participation mark and your negotiation mark, sometimes if you get a great deal, then your negotiation mark will be high for this exercise.
sections.teaching: His teaching is funny and interesting, probably the most relaxing lesson in the semester, and he will share lots of interning stories with you. And most of the time will be put in the negotiation with classmates, and he will teach back the case and skills the lesson after.
sections.grading: The grading is good, if you didn't miss any negotiation, and do okay in the negotiation and have two exams above 0.5-1 SD, probably can get a range.
sections.workload:
Just need to read cases one week before the negotiation lesson, and he will give a mini quiz about the case, but just very simple and easy, then you just negotiate with classmates.
Two exams in total, and just study the notes is fine.
No project and assignments!!!

sections.content:
useful and practical content. talks about useful skill to be adopted in different types of negotiation (salary negotiation, cross-cultural negotiation, dispute, and so on)
The cases are really interesting and help you be involved in content because you actually have to fight for your side to get better results.
sections.teaching:
I think he is the only professor that makes me get excited for my class. I always waited for Tuesdays and Thursdays just to hear him make fun of students with strange negotiation results. He also has many experiences and useful skills that he shares with students.
His lecturers make the time fly by and his slides are organized (but often really repetitive)
sections.grading:
35 % midterm
35% finals
30 % participation

Even though I participated a lot in class and did not miss a single class, I got a B because of my midterm and final grades. He has really tough grading criteria for his exams (like if you miss a specific word in your explanation, you will get your marks off)
69 out of 100 for midterm (exact average)
71 out of 100 for final (exact average)
participated a lot in class.
sections.workload:
Only a one or two page long case to be read every week. Do read and attend class because you actually need to negotiate with your partner(s) every week and this counts toward your final grade a lot.
Exams are the frustrating parts because the content is so easy to understand and vague that you never know how to prepare for the exams. Reading textbook does not seem to help that much (The book has too much content to be read)

sections.content: This course focuses on the techniques for different types of negotiation, like disputes and salary negotiation. There is one negotiation exercise every week, in which you can build up your negotiation skills and apply what you have learned in the lessons.
sections.teaching: Professor Nason's teaching is lively and interactive! He always tells us some interesting stories when he is illustrating the negotiation techniques. He loves to interact with students and it definitely brings up the teaching atmosphere.
sections.grading: The grading is really good. I got an A for this course, even thoguh my mid-term and final exam results were above mean by around 0.5 sd only.
sections.workload: The workload is very light for this course. You just have to read the assigned case every week and participate in the negotiation exercise. Besides one mid-term exam and one final exam, there is only one assignment due in the end of the course. The assignment is easy indeed- an A4 size personal negotiation guide.

sections.content: The content was interesting and useful. I am sure I will apply some of the things, which I have learned, when negotiating in the future.
sections.teaching: Professor Nason was very engaging. His classes were never boring and his lectures were very straightforward.
sections.grading: Grading wasn't harsh at all. If you do your readings you will be fine. Make sure you understand all the concepts before exams tough because some of the questions are tricky.
sections.workload: You have to read a case before each lecture and prepare for the exams. There isn't too much work.

sections.content: This course gives you great information about different negotiation strategies in the business world. It includes many different strategies and different techniques in order to gain the upper hand in business deals. It also teaches you to create scenarios that benefit both parties and can be used in all different aspects of life. I fundamentally enjoyed the content as a majority of it was non-theoretical and very practical. There are a lot of in class negotiations which i feel really highlighted the concepts. This course offers an opportunity to really interact with peers in class which is something that i really found lacking in HKUST.
sections.teaching: Mr. Nason is one of the aspects that makes this course as incredible as it is. He was always very helpful and used different mediums of teaching which is perfect for both visual, practical and theoretical learners alike. He is a very open teacher and is more than happy to help out with concepts that may not be clear. He is a great teacher and has really made this course incredible.
sections.grading: In terms of grading, this course was fairly easy for me. I really enjoyed the teaching style and the different negotiation methods taught which probably contributed to the A i received. As long as you understand the concepts and have had practice applying them (which you should have if you attend the classes) you should be completely fine in both the final and the midterm exam. The final exams focus more on situations and how to adapt the negotiation styles to them. It is important to attend classes as well because the in class negotiation results are recorded and will be leveraged into your final grade through some percentage.
sections.workload: The workload in this course was very low. After each class, you receive a scenario for the next class which you should read up on and study (however they are usually 1-2 pages long so it isnt much reading to get through). I had a lot of time to focus on other courses during the semester and found that the majority of the learning was in class.

sections.content: The content is very useful. It involves lots of real life examples and negotiation skills.
sections.teaching: The Professor is very friendly, knowledgeable and funny. Interactive learning and case studies are used. Active participation is encouraged. Do expect to speak a lot in class.
sections.grading: Grades are mainly determined by two exams and class participation.There are also quizzes on the weekly case assignments.
sections.workload: Preparation is a must. Everyone needs to read one case assignment every week. Only two exams and weekly negotiations on different case studies. No projects or written assignments.

sections.content: The content is base on the book "The Mind and Heart of the Negotiator". Each week there will be two class, one for negotiation of a case with an assigned role and the other class for debriefing for the last negotiation. You will be able to have a lot of hands on experience on negotiating a lot of different things in many different format.
sections.teaching:
Professor Nason has been teaching in UST for over 20 years, and he is excellent in story telling. The class is usually engaging and thought provoking.

He will also include lots of stories from his personal experience to illustrate the theories mentioned in class.
sections.grading:
Grading are mainly determined by mid term and final exam, which consist of MC questions and short case for the short question part.

There are also some quiz regarding to the case distributed.

Class participation marks are also one of the grading criteria.
sections.workload: Every week there will be a case distributed, and you will need to prepare it for the quiz and the negotiation itself. It will be a choice to prepare more or less, depends on your personal will. The bottom line is the more preparation you did, the better chance you have in succeeding the negotiations.

sections.content: This course is quite a fun one to take. On a weekly basis, you get a new case to then negotiate when coming back to class for an entire hour. The other class is spent discussing on the case and seeing how everyone could have done better.
sections.teaching: The professor for this course is a really great one. I was looking forward to that course every week.
sections.workload: Little workload for this course. Probably one or two hours a week if it isn't to study for mid-terms or finals.
